module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1121

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1121](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1121)
- [BeLi16] Bezdek, Károly and Litvak, Alexander E., *Packing convex bodies by cylinders*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. (2016), 725-738.
- [GoGo45] Goodman, A. W. and Goodman, R. E., *A circle covering theorem*. Amer. Math. Monthly
  (1945), 494-498.
- [Ha47] Hadwiger, H., *Nonseparable convex systems*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1947), 583-585.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1121

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/--
If $C_1,\ldots,C_n$ are circles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no line
disjoint from all the circles divides them into two non-empty sets then the circles can be
covered by a circle of radius $r=\sum r_i$.

This is true, and was proved by Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] (whose proof also generalises to
higher dimensions). A generalisation to convex bodies was proved by Hadwiger [Ha47].

An alternative proof is given by Bezdek and Litvak [BeLi16].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1121.lean"]
theorem erdos_1121 {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ²) (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : ℝ²) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : ℝ², (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i) := by
  sorry

/--
The proof of Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] also generalises to higher dimensions: if
$B_1,\ldots,B_n$ are balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no hyperplane
disjoint from all the balls divides them into two non-empty sets then the balls can be covered by
a ball of radius $r=\sum r_i$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_1121.variants.higher_dimension {d n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1121

reformulations.difference: The source's hypothesis says that no line disjoint from all the circles divides them into two non-empty sets. The Lean encodes it as `hsep`: for every `v ≠ 0` and `t`, if the line {p | ⟪v,p⟫ = t} misses every `Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)`, then all *centres* lie strictly on one side: `(∀ i, ⟪v,c i⟫ < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < ⟪v,c i⟫)`. So it records the side of each centre, not of each whole disk.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every line in ℝ² has the form {⟪v,·⟫ = t} with v ≠ 0. Suppose a closed ball misses the line and has a point p on the other side from its centre c. The point of the segment [c,p] where ⟪v,·⟫ = t lies in the ball by convexity, a contradiction. So each such ball lies in the open half-plane containing its centre. Hence 'all centres on one side' holds iff the line does not place a whole disk in each open half-plane, i.e. does not divide the disks into two non-empty sets. I proved `HsepFC c r ↔ HsepLit c r` in Lean for positive radii in any `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`, where `HsepLit` is `¬ ∃ i j, closedBall (c i) (r i) ⊆ {p | ⟪v,p⟫ < t} ∧ closedBall (c j) (r j) ⊆ {p | t < ⟪v,p⟫}`. I also checked that `erdos_1121` applies directly under `HsepLit` via this iff.

reformulations.difference: "Circles" are modelled as closed Euclidean disks `Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)` in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` with `0 < r i`. "Can be covered by a circle of radius ∑ r_i" becomes inclusion of the union of the disks in a closed disk `Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i)`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If a line meets a closed disk, it meets the boundary circle: a line through the interior crosses the boundary, and a line cannot lie inside a bounded disk. So 'line disjoint from the circle' is the same as 'line disjoint from the closed disk'. By convexity, a disk contains a circle iff it contains the closed disk the circle bounds. This closed-disk reading is the standard one. Bezdek–Litvak define non-separable families for 'closed circular disks', with lines that divide the disks 'without touching or intersecting at least one disk'. Akopyan–Balitskiy–Grigorev, following Hadwiger, use compact convex bodies. An open-disk reading would let tangent lines separate and would give a strictly weaker theorem. The file uses the standard, stronger version, and I verified it is true.

reformulations.difference: The variant uses the same centre-side encoding for hyperplanes {⟪v,·⟫ = t}, v ≠ 0, in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`. It is stated for every d, including d = 0 (no hyperplanes, so it is trivially true) and d = 1 (Goodman's segment lemma).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The Lean-proved lemma `HsepFC ↔ HsepLit` holds for every d, so `hsep` says exactly that no hyperplane disjoint from all the closed balls divides them into two non-empty sets. This is also equivalent to Hadwiger's non-separability, as used in Akopyan–Balitskiy–Grigorev Theorem 1.1 (every hyperplane meeting the convex hull of the union meets a member). A hyperplane that misses every ball and does not separate them leaves the convex hull in one open half-space, and conversely. The low-dimensional cases d = 0 and d = 1 are true, so including them does not change the claim.

review.notes:
No findings: both declarations state the claims the source poses, and both are true, non-vacuous and sharp.

Lean checks (scratch files in /workspace/review):

(1) Main theorem (plby_scratch2.lean). The linked formal proof (plby/lean-proofs, written for v4.29.1) compiles against this repo's Mathlib v4.33.1 after one local fix. A `convert` in `sorted_weighted_sum_le` produced an extra instance goal; I rewrote that step. A short bridge then proves a theorem whose type is `rfl`-equal to `Erdos1121.erdos_1121`. It depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. So the `formal_proof` record is accurate.

(2) Variant (hd_scratch.lean). The internal part of that proof never uses dimension 2. Generalised to `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`, it proves the exact type of `erdos_1121.variants.higher_dimension` for all d, with standard axioms only. This agrees with its `research solved` tag and with the source's remark that the proof 'generalises to higher dimensions' (Akopyan–Balitskiy–Grigorev state it for ℝ^d).

(3) Non-vacuity and sharpness (tight.lean). Two touching unit disks, centred at 0 and 2e₁, satisfy `hsep`. No closed ball of radius below ∑ r = 2 covers their union. So the hypothesis can hold non-trivially and the bound ∑ r_i is attained.

(4) `hsep` encoding (hsep_iff.lean). The centre-side form is equivalent to the literal 'a whole disk in each open half-plane' reading, in any dimension.

Status: the source records 'PROVED (LEAN)', which matches `research solved` plus the `formal_proof` link. No status issue.

Not accessed: the original Goodman–Goodman (1945) and Hadwiger (1947) papers; the publisher pages returned 403. Their content as used here is reported consistently by Akopyan–Balitskiy–Grigorev and by Bezdek–Litvak. The docstring's Hadwiger remark ('a generalisation to convex bodies') is copied from erdosproblems.com and is not formalised, so it does not affect either statement.

The module docstring's bibliographic data for [BeLi16], [GoGo45] and [Ha47] are correct (volume numbers omitted).
